relevance.rationale: JOIN CONFIRMED from front matter: the document self-identifies as arXiv:2111.06645v3 with the journal volume and article number recorded on the registered entry, and its title and author pair match. LOAD-BEARING AND VERIFIED AGAINST THE SOURCE at the tightest locator in this slice. lean/QOU/QBeta/GZWeightSelection.lean:32 and lean/QOU/QBeta/GZWeightGeneral.lean:31 both cite 'eq. 3.7' and define kappa(sigma_0) = 3/2, kappa(non-trivial) = 0. I read eq. (3.7) in the source: the weight kappa(sigma) of a representation sigma in P_K is defined to be 3/2 if sigma = sigma_0 and 0 otherwise. That is verbatim what the Lean encodes, and the surrounding eq. (3.6) is the generalized quantum modularity conjecture whose automorphy factor (cX+d)^(-kappa(sigma)) is what makes kappa a weight — so GZWeightGeneral's knot-independent kappaGZ is a faithful generalisation, since (3.7) is stated for all sigma in P_K and not only for 4_1. The two .md citations also check out: mass-endomorphism/channel-rotation-askey-lit.md:30 claims the state integral factors into a q-series and a q-tilde series with leading asymptotics tracing Vol + i*CS, and the source supports both halves (restrictions to C minus R factorize bilinearly as finite sums of products of a q-series and a q-tilde series; the leading asymptotic exponent of the new matrices involves the complex volume); mass-endomorphism/complex-volume-character-variety-path.md:19 uses it only as consistency framing, which is within scope. The files' own discipline notes — that the weight values are the cited definition and the selection rules are their algebraic consequences, no fit — are accurate.
